'''''Camellia petelotii''''' is a species of [[plant]] in the family [[Theaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{Cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:829954-1 |title=POWO: ''Camellia petelotii'' (Merr.) Sealy (retrieved 24 March 2021) |access-date=17 February 2023 |archive-date=3 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203160759/https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:829954-1 |url-status=live }}</ref> It is found in [[China]] (endemic in the [[Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region]] in southern China) and [[Vietnam]]. It is known as the '''golden camellia''' for its distinctive yellow blossoms. Synonyms include ''C. chrysantha'' and '''''Camellia nitidissima'''''. The golden camellia originated 170 million years ago, and is a first-class nationally protected plant in China.<ref name=taiwantrade>{{Cite web |url = https://info.taiwantrade.com/biznews/%E5%BB%A3%E8%A5%BF%E7%89%B9%E8%89%B2%E9%A3%9F%E5%93%81-%E9%87%91%E8%8A%B1%E8%8C%B6%E4%BB%8B%E7%B4%B9-930835.html |title = 廣西特色食品—金花茶介紹 |publisher = 中華民國對外貿易發展協會 |language = zh |access-date = 16 November 2022 |archive-date = 16 November 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221116081648/https://info.taiwantrade.com/biznews/%E5%BB%A3%E8%A5%BF%E7%89%B9%E8%89%B2%E9%A3%9F%E5%93%81-%E9%87%91%E8%8A%B1%E8%8C%B6%E4%BB%8B%E7%B4%B9-930835.html |url-status = live }}</ref> The golden camellia is extremely demanding on the growth environment, its genes are extremely difficult to replicate, and, once transplanted, it is known to die or genetically mutate.<ref name=taiwantrade/> It is also threatened by [[habitat loss]]. Therefore, in 1986, the Golden Camellia National Nature Reserve was built in Fangcheng, [[Guangxi]], with a total area of 9195.1 hectares.<ref>{{Cite web |url = http://sthjt.gxzf.gov.cn/zfxxgk/zfxxgkgl/fdzdgknr/sthj/t3630484.shtml |title = 广西防城金花茶自然保护区简介 |publisher = 广西壮族自治区生态环境厅 |language = zh |access-date = 16 November 2022 |archive-date = 16 November 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221116081628/http://sthjt.gxzf.gov.cn/zfxxgk/zfxxgkgl/fdzdgknr/sthj/t3630484.shtml |url-status = live }}</ref>

In southern China and Vietnam where the golden camellia originates, it has been used to make tea, and in addition has been propagated as a garden plant for its waxy yellow flowers, which are notably unusual for a member of the ''[[Camellia]]'' genus. The plant is endangered in the wild, but is widely favored in gardens.

== Description ==
'''''Camellia petelotii''''' is a shrub or small tree growing up to 5 meters in height.<ref>{{Cite web |url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242310160 |title = Camellia petelotii (Merrill) Sealy, Kew Bull. |publisher = Flora of China |language = en |access-date = 17 November 2022 |archive-date = 27 September 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220927141718/http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242310160 |url-status = live }}</ref>

== Uses ==
With Golden Camellias, Chinese experts have been conducting experiments to create new varieties of the flower. Experts have found a few and named them, "''Nayue Hongyan''", "''Liaoyan Beauty''", "''Xinhuang''" and other names, which have contributed to the new tea market.<ref name=tangzou/> According to the research and experiments of The Institute of Medicinal Plant Development (China)-Guangxi Branch and some other Chinese medicine research institutions in Guangxi, Golden camellia tea has the functions of preventing cancer, inhibiting tumor growth, lowering blood pressure, lowering blood lipids, lowering cholesterol, preventing atherosclerosis, delaying aging and other health effects as improve the body's immune.<ref name=taiwantrade/>
